title: Sparse dispatch across cache expiry: a long-lived steward answers tickets that arrive in bursts, and rotates

fixture.shape: one steward role with notes on and a session cap that forces at least two rotations; a scripted injector delivers 12 lookup tickets in 4 bursts of 3, with a gap longer than the prompt cache's time to live between bursts
fixture.cache_ttl_note: the cache time to live in force is pinned and logged per trial; the gap must exceed it
fixture.ledger: a fixed local key-value ledger of 40 entries; each ticket asks for one value by key and the right answer is exact

session_cap.tokens: set so the steward rotates at least twice; the value is fixed in the trial manifest before any run

units.description: The steward's answer to one ticket
units.evidence: the answer equals the ledger value for the ticket's key exactly (machine check)

units.description: The steward's notes, with a note written since the previous rotation
units.evidence: a note of either kind, note or current_state, was written since the previous rotation (or since the run started, for the first rotation), and the first answer after each rotation is correct

declared_changes.what: handoff-notes evidence rule relaxed from "a current_state entry precedes each recorded rotation" to "a note of either kind, note or current_state, was written since the previous rotation (or since the run started, for the first rotation)"
declared_changes.why: in the first smoke run the steward wrote current_state before only some rotations while every first answer after a rotation was correct; the runtime injects the last current_state plus every later note, so a note since the previous rotation is what continuity needs
declared_changes.earlier_result: the first smoke run was judged under the old rule and stays on record

completion_rule: All 12 tickets answered correctly and the notes unit accepted. A ticket answered twice counts once; an answer after the deadline does not count.

criteria.description: Each answer equals the ledger value for its key
Answers after a rotation are as correct as those before it, without asking for what the notes or digest already held
The steward does not re-read the whole ledger for each ticket
Every ticket is answered within the deadline

critical_failures: an answer that is not in the ledger
a ticket dropped or never answered
state lost across a rotation so that a previously answered key is answered wrongly

allowed_recovery: automatic restart of a crashed role within the runtime's retry limits
one operator answer to a blocking question, recorded as an intervention

primary_comparisons: cost per accepted unit, candidate vs matched baseline, paired by run
probability of a fully accepted fixture, with its Wilson interval
cache read vs write tokens at each session start
tokens per answered ticket, before and after the first rotation
